prompt: OPTIONAL How the Rugby Game Works Rugby union is usually played on a grass-covered pitch 100 metres long and 70 metres wide (see diagram below). Each team has 15 players and a game lasts for 80 minutes. The game is played with an oval-shaped ball that players can kick, run with, or pass to teammates in order to score tries or kick goals.To score a try, worth five points, a player must carry the ball across the opposition's try line and ground it. His team's best kicker can then earn two more points for the conversion if he kicks the ball between the goalposts and over the crossbar. But scoring a try is not so easy. When an attacking team's players are running with the ball towards the try line, they are faced with a line of big, strong defenders who are experts at tackling. To get past these defenders, attacking players can pass the ball to each other until one of them finds a gap in the defence through which they can run to score a try. The ball can only be passed backwards or sideways, however; a forward pass is a foul that the referee should penalize.

title: Task 1
prompt: Vocabulary Boost: Cultural Sensitivity and Global Sports Communication Cultural sensitivity means being careful and respectful when dealing with people from different cultures. Example: Cultural sensitivity helps teams from different countries work well together. Customs are traditional ways of doing things in a particular country. Example: In some countries, it is a custom to bow instead of shaking hands. Etiquette refers to polite rules for how to behave in social or official situations. Example: Good etiquette is important during opening ceremonies and official dinners. Protocol is the official set of rules followed in formal events. Example: Before international matches, teams follow a strict protocol, like lining up and hearing the national anthem. Respect means showing politeness and kindness to others, especially those who are different from you. Example: Athletes should always show respect to referees and players from other teams.

title: Task 5
prompt: Reading Text: Football Without Borders Football is the world’s most popular sport, played and watched by millions of people in every country. In international football, teams and officials come from many different cultures. To play and work together well, they must show cultural sensitivity. This means respecting different customs, gestures, and ways of communicating. For example, in some countries, it is polite to bow, while in others, players shake hands. Some teams pray before a match, and others sing loudly. Coaches and referees must understand these differences to avoid misunderstandings. During the World Cup, the host country welcomes teams from all over the world. They follow strict protocol for starting matches, greeting officials, and playing the national anthems. Good etiquette is important in post-match press conferences and media interviews. Players must also follow a code of conduct, showing respect to referees and fans. Interpreters often help teams from different countries communicate during training and games. One example is the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. The organizers trained volunteers and referees on cultural differences and provided information in many languages. Another case is the UEFA Champions League, where multinational teams work together every day and learn how to respect each other’s traditions. Football is more than a game—it is a global language that connects people. But to play it well, we must learn how to communicate across cultures.
